0.0.n: This is the beginning of the name もなみ, not the particle も.

0.1.n: This completes the name もなみ; it is not a separate word here.

0.2.n: ちゃん follows a name to show affection or familiarity, often when addressing a child.

1.0.n: 今 tells us when the cooking is happening.

1.1.n: お料理してる shortens お料理している, showing an ongoing action; お adds a polite touch to 料理.

1.2.n: から follows the cooking statement to give the reason for the warning.

1.3.n: 危ない describes the situation as unsafe, without specifying exactly what poses the danger.

1.4.n: よ draws the listener’s attention to the warning; ー shows the sound being drawn out.

0.tip: もなみ is one name despite the word split, and ちゃん adds affection.

1.lit: Now, because I'm cooking, it's dangerous, you know.
1.tip: から attaches to the reason: the cooking explains why the situation is dangerous.
